topStory.headline: NBC News: Students Use 'Humanizer' Tools to Avoid A.I. Detection False Positives
topStory.summary:
Students are turning to A.I. tools called "humanizers" to make their work less likely to be flagged by A.I. detection software, even when they have not used A.I. to write their papers, according to NBC News reporter Tyler Kingkade. Turnitin has identified 150 A.I. humanizer tools, some charging up to $50 per subscription. In October alone, 43 of these humanizers tracked by Turnitin had 33.9 million combined website visits.

Research cited in the article found that Turnitin's detection tool failed to identify more than 25% of A.I.-generated or A.I.-rephrased texts. Erin Ramirez, an associate professor at California State University, Monterey Bay, told NBC News: "Students now are trying to prove that they're human, even though they might have never touched AI ever. So where are we? We're just in a spiral that will never end." She also noted: "It's almost like the better the writer you are, the more AI thinks you're AI."

Students have faced academic discipline over A.I. detection accusations, with lawsuits filed at Yale University and Adelphi University. At the University at Buffalo, more than 1,500 students signed a petition against A.I. detector software. Tricia Bertram Gallant, director of the Academic Integrity Office at UC San Diego, told NBC News: "If it's an unsupervised assessment, don't bother trying to ban AI. And don't bother trying to prove AI was used because you end up spending more time doing that."

stories.headline: Writing Faculty Assert Right to Refuse A.I. in Classrooms
stories.summary: The Conference on College Composition and Communication passed a resolution affirming students' and faculty's right to decline generative A.I. in writing classrooms, according to Inside Higher Ed. The report states that 15% of faculty report their institutions mandate A.I. use, while 81% report required use of learning management systems with embedded A.I. tools they cannot disable.

stories.headline: UK Survey: 75% of A.I.-Using Students Fear Wrongful Flagging
stories.summary: A YouGov survey of 2,373 UK students found that 75% of those using A.I. tools feel stressed about being wrongfully flagged for plagiarism by detection tools, according to Times Higher Education. Universities UK chief executive Vivienne Stern called for institutions to "reconsider detection tools that give false positives."

stories.headline: Washington University Launches +A.I. Academic Initiative
stories.summary: Washington University in St. Louis launched +A.I., an academic initiative led by Provost Mark D. West to integrate artificial intelligence into teaching, learning, and research, according to WashU Source. The initiative includes an A.I. literacy module for undergraduates and an A.I. Curriculum Corps to support faculty in developing A.I.-integrated courses.
